task: EXT-F-1003-T40 automatic page-load scrape behavior preparation

source_findings.setting_and_trigger: src/hooks/use-auto-scrape.ts reads scrapeAutoOnLoad and invokes captureWithFallback for the active HTTP(S) page after a 600ms settle delay.
source_findings.readback: ContextRulesComposerChip builds a no-send preview through the same buildChatContextValues path as a turn. With manual capture absent, a unique marker on a fresh controlled page after enabling can establish the causal automatic capture effect. The v2 preview also represents page_full_content as a structured value when present; its complete rendered values can distinguish an absent content entry from a failed/incomplete preview.
source_findings.default_context_shape: src/lib/chat/context/shape-config.ts defaults to v2-bundled. That builder emits page_full_content for a trustworthy scrape; it does not emit scrape provenance. The legacy scrape_source key in v1-flat is unnecessary for the causal enabled check and should not be added to the retiring shape.
source_findings.missing_trigger: The existing Settings native runner has no adapter that opens the no-send context preview and reads the complete v2 values for a unique fresh-page ON check and an explicit absent-page_full_content OFF check over a bounded sample window. This is a harness coverage gap, not evidence of a product defect. Direct inFlight/current-store instrumentation is unnecessary for that route.

gaps: Add a native adapter that reads the complete ContextRules v2 preview, confirms fresh active document identity, checks the ON unique marker with manual capture absent, and checks page_full_content remains absent while OFF across a bounded observation window.
A bounded OFF window only supports absence during the observed interval; it does not prove no later capture ever occurs.
No helper tests or native acceptance are claimed in this preparation.
scope_note: The adapter-model helper and tests from 5967a7ca were removed because their required runtime fields are not exposed by the current app.
